title: fix(fields): a lookup value hydrated from a bare id is labelled from the schema once it arrives (objectui#10487)
body:
Fixes #10487
Clause-②: no

A lookup that mounts already holding a bare id now labels its chip from the referenced object's schema once that schema arrives. Before, when the record fetch won the race against `getObjectSchema`, the chip kept the no-schema label (the `name` guess) for good, while the dropdown option for the same record read the declared `nameField`.

## Reproduction (base `db3896c4c`, the card's fixture)

Value `'c1'`; the object's `nameField` is `contract_no`; the row is `{ id: 'c1', name: 'Acme', contract_no: 'HT-001' }`. The pin's backend holds `getObjectSchema` open until the chip is labelled, then releases it.

| reading | base | head |
|---|---|---|
| mounted chip, before the schema | `Acme` | `Acme` |
| mounted chip, after the schema | `Acme` | `HT-001` |
| dropdown option for `c1` | `HT-001` | `HT-001` |
| chip after picking `c1` again | `HT-001` | `HT-001` |

The mechanism, confirmed at source: the hydration effect built each option with `recordToOption` inside its async fetch, using the `refObjectSchema` of the render it ran in (`null`), and cached the BUILT option in `pickerResolvedRecords`. `findOption` then found the id in that cache, so every later run of the effect returned early and nothing rebuilt the label.

## The change: keep the RECORD, derive the label (one derivation)

`packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx` only.

- The hydration effect fetches rows and builds no option. It merges them into a new `hydratedRecords` state, keyed by `recordValue` (the value expression `recordToOption` already used, now one helper both read).
- `hydratedOptions` is a memo that maps those rows through `recordToOption` with the same inputs the dropdown's `fetchedOptions` uses: the declared `displayField`, `idField`, the description field, `refObjectSchema`, and the field-read gate of the current policy. It re-derives when any of them changes, so the chip follows the schema when it arrives.
- `findOption` and `findOptionLoose` consult static, fetched, picked (`pickerResolvedRecords`), then hydrated options. A pick outranks the hydrated row for the same value, as it did when the two shared one cache and the later write won.
- The effect's dependency list drops `declaredDisplayField` and `effectiveDescriptionField`, which the effect no longer reads. The eslint disable stays. The reads it hides shrank from `dataSource`, `findOption`, `perms`, `refObjectSchema` to `dataSource`, `findOption` (the `--no-inline-config` message, base vs head).

No `key=` remount, and no re-fetch on the schema's arrival.

### Why this route and not the other two

- Relabel on arrival (an effect on `refObjectSchema` that rebuilds the cached options) needs the rows anyway. An option cannot be rebuilt from itself: `recordToOption` spreads the record over `label`, so the old label would win the spread. That route is this change plus an effect, and an extra render that still shows the stale label.
- Defer labelling until the schema is known needs a "schema settled" state (`getObjectSchema` can be absent, can reject, or can be slow). Every chip would wait on the metadata call, and it still needs a re-run path. It is larger, and slower for the user.
- Keeping the record is the pattern the recents rail in the same file already uses (`recentRows` state, `recentOptions` memo).

### Fetch count, measured

| ordering | base `findOne` calls | head |
|---|---|---|
| record first, schema later (the card) | 1 | 1 |
| schema arrives while the record fetch is in flight | 2 | 1 |

On base the second ordering got the right label only by accident. The schema's arrival changed `effectiveDescriptionField` (it derives from the schema's columns), which re-ran the effect, cancelled the fetch in flight and issued a second one after the schema was known.

### `handleSelect` and the hydrated path

Both build the label through `recordToOption` with the same inputs, so they agree once the schema is known: the pin's pick control and the mounted chip both read `HT-001`. The pick path still caches a BUILT option, so a pick made before the schema arrives keeps the no-schema label. That is measured and reported under Acceptance notes; it is not changed here.

### A second input follows too: the policy

The effect used to capture the field-read gate of the policy in force when it ran (objectui#10373). The memo reads the current one. So a field the policy denies after the chip is labelled (a policy that loads late) leaves the chip's label, as it leaves the dropdown's. Pinned as row 4.

## Pin: `LookupField.hydratedLabel-10487.test.tsx`

| # | row | base | head |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | single hydrated id: the chip reads `HT-001` after the schema; `findOne` once | red, `Acme` | green |
| 2 | batched `$in` path: the chips read `HT-001`, `HT-002`; one `$in` query | red, `Acme`, `Initech` | green |
| 3 | the schema arrives while the fetch is in flight: chip `HT-001`, `findOne` once | red, 2 calls | green |
| 4 | a field denied after the chip is labelled leaves the label (`c1`) | red, `Acme` | green |
| 5 | control: the dropdown option reads `HT-001` | green | green |
| 6 | control: picking `c1` leaves the chip on `HT-001` | green | green |

Rows 1 and 2 also assert the chip read `Acme` before the schema was released, so the fixture's ordering is proven, not assumed.

## Ablations (one-shot, at `011676680`, restored by blob)

A1 and A3 ran through `../objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hit exactly once, the blob changed, and the restore was proven (blob equal to HEAD's, `git diff HEAD` empty). A2 checked out the base blob and restored the HEAD blob under a trap, proven the same way. The pin imports `./LookupField` directly, so no `dist` is involved.

- A1, the derivation frozen: the `hydratedOptions` memo keyed on the rows alone, so the label is built once, when the rows land. Predicted and observed: rows 1, 2 and 4 red; rows 3, 5 and 6 green (3 failed, 3 passed).
- A3, the dependency list: the effect's deps regain `declaredDisplayField` and `effectiveDescriptionField`. Predicted and observed: row 3 red (`findOne` called 2 times), the rest green (1 failed, 5 passed).
- A2, the whole file at base `db3896c4c` (blob `7593aeb`; restored to HEAD blob `3054087`): rows 1 to 4 red, the two controls green (4 failed, 2 passed).

## Verification (HEAD `011676680`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/fields/` from the repo root: 198 files passed and 1 skipped, of 199 (the tracked test files under `packages/fields` also number 199); 3272 tests passed, 7 skipped.
- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/fields^...' run build`, then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the pin.
- eslint on the two touched files, per rule, base vs head: `LookupField.tsx` is equal in every rule (`react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` 3 and 3, or 5 and 5 with `--no-inline-config`; `no-explicit-any` 37 and 37). The pin has no messages.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `pnpm check:changeset-claims` (nothing flagged; its born-false leg found no line address to judge), `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, and `check:test-path-roots`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:shell-escape-residue`: all exit 0.
- NOT MEASURED: CI, and a browser run (the pin drives the real widget in happy-dom).

Changeset: `@object-ui/fields` patch.

## Acceptance notes

- A behaviour change beyond the chip label: a browse-all (`RecordPickerDialog`) pick replaced `pickerResolvedRecords` wholesale, and that also dropped the hydrated entries. Hydrated rows now live in their own state and survive it. The dialog's records still win for the ids they carry.
- A finding, reported to the seat and not filed here: a pick made in the dropdown BEFORE the schema arrives keeps the no-schema label. Measured on head `011676680` with a throwaway probe: options before the schema `Acme`, `Initech`; the chip after the pick `Acme`; the chip after the schema `Acme`; the options after the schema `HT-001`, `HT-002`. `handleSelect` caches the built option it is handed, and the row behind it is not kept, so changing that is a design step, not a mechanical one. The browse-all dialog path (`handlePickerSelectRecords`) builds options the same way and was not measured.
